title.narrative: Climate-Friendly Agribusiness Value Chains Sector Project (Supplemental Financing)

description.narrative: The proposed project supports the implementation of the government's Agriculture Development Strategy to 2025 (ADS) by boosting the competitiveness of rice value chains in Khammouane, Saravan, and Savannakhet provinces, and vegetable value chains in Vientiane Capital, Champasak, and Sekong provinces. The project will improve the climate resilience of agricultural infrastructure, and enhance crop productivity, diversification, and commercialization. It will help improve the capacity for storage, processing, quality, and safety testing, and promote the use of biofertilizers and organic farming. It will strengthen the capacity of farmers and agribusinesses for climate-smart agriculture (CSA), and create an enabling environment for climate-friendly agribusinesses to promote sustainability along the value chain.

Output: Climate-smart agriculture and agribusiness promoted Indicator: Knowledge and skills of 20,000 farmers in CSA, organic farming, and agribusiness increased Achievement: 18504 Progress/Status: CSA and GAP/Organic Training - Over 22,878 farmers including 7,185 women, trained via CSA/Organic/GAP training sessions (PPIUs/DPIUs with CS1 support). 7,948 farmers trained specifically on agribusiness topics by DAEC, with 496 officers attending agribusiness TOTs (some overlap). CSA Demonstration Plots - 631 plots established (590 for rice, 41 for vegetables), targeting ~3,600 farmers. Training Materials - Revised capacity building plan prepared. - CSA, GAP, and Organic training manuals updated and adapted to local needs. - Videos, leaflets, and posters developed for dissemination (e.g., dry direct seeding, rice broadcasting, postharvest techniques). Gender and CSA Events - Gender & CSA awareness events: 1,512 villagers participated (807 women, 53% female participation). APG Registration - 159 APGs officially registered out of 214 supported. Monitoring - Outcome survey for farmer training launched (Jan-Feb 2025) with 503 farmers interviewed across 56 villages in 11 districts (Report completed and submitted).
Data Source: PPMS reports; capacity building master plan monitoring report

Output: Climate-smart agriculture and agribusiness promoted Indicator: Two additional climate-resilient varieties of rice and vegetables released Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Rice Varieties - Field trials ongoing at research stations and demonstration plots. - Varieties tested include HTDK15, HTDK16, HTDK17, HXBF-BPH1, HXBF-BB, BL154 and TDK8 (control). - NAFRI (National Agriculture and Forestry Research Institute) is leading rice variety testing in Savannakhet and Khammouane provinces. Vegetable Varieties - World Vegetable Center (WorldVeg) contracted in April 2025 to lead the vegetable variety development program. - Initial planning and action plan development have started between WorldVeg, NAFRI, DAEC, and PIC. Field Demonstrations - Rice variety demonstrations underway, including heat-tolerant varieties. - Ongoing trials at cash crop and rice research centers. Planned Activities - Continue field testing and demonstrations of rice varieties. - Develop action plan and begin demonstration of climate-resilient vegetable varieties in target provinces. subsequently registered for commercial production. It is reported that NAFRI distributed climate resilient rice varieties in all project provinces in October 2023.
Support on development of suitable vegetable varieties is under negotiation with the World Veg; a revised proposal is to be submitted by 15 July 2024 that includes all four priority crops (cabbage, chilli, spring onion and tomato). World Veg will work with NAFRI and local officials to develop a vegetable supply calendar to help understand the peaks and troughs of supply throughout the year and will assist pilot cooperatives in pack house design and operation to improve product and post-harvest handling to include simple storage techniques such as drying and ambient temperature storge options. Data Source: PPMS reports; capacity building master plan monitoring report

Output: Enabling environment for climate-friendly agribusiness enhanced. Indicator: At least 25 APGs entered into agribusiness ventures Achievement: 6 Progress/Status: - Currently, 159 out of 214 selected Agricultural Production Groups (APGs) have been officially registered. These groups have been engaged in various capacity-building activities and smallholder financing support through the project. However, there is no confirmation that at least 25 APGs have formally entered into agribusiness ventures yet.
During last QR (jan-mar 2025), we indicated: - 43 APGs have expressed interest in developing agribusiness activities - 22 APGs have expressed interest in merging into six cooperatives - 5 APGs registered as separate cooperatives: - Agriculture competitiveness cooperative of Kongtoun village in Paksong district, Champasak - New model cooperative focusing on agriculture of Lakkhao village in Thataeng district, Sekong - Joint cooperative of Nongsai-Pholern villages in Saravan district, Saravan; and - Agriculture Development Cooperative of Teung village, Xebangfay district, Khammouane) - Rice quality of Thonghab, Xaybouly District, Savannakhet province. - In summary, while progress has been made on registering APGs and providing them with support, the targets of 25 APGs entering agribusiness ventures and 5 becoming cooperatives have not yet been fully achieved. Further support and structured facilitation are needed to transition APGs into cooperatives and formal agribusiness partnerships
Data Source: PPMS reports; Mekong Business Forum reports
